item.title: The Price Of ‘Free Speech’: Grok AI And The Escalation Of Digital Misogyny
item.description: Deepfake images that Grok AI generated have severe social, psychological, and career-based implications for women. The post The Price Of ‘Free Speech’: Grok AI And The Escalation Of Digital Misogyny appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Rape As Statecraft: How India’s Political Weapon Shapes Women’s Future
item.description: From religious scriptures to "entertainment," India's elected representatives continue to justify rape, revealing how sexual violence functions as a deliberate political tool. The post Rape As Statecraft: How India’s Political Weapon Shapes Women’s Future appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: As Iranians Fight Their Far-Right Government, A Narrative War Brews Elsewhere
item.description: While Iranians are mounting a brave fight against an authoritarian regime and a crumbling economy, a narrative war that leverages this critical struggle for ulterior motives is being fought in other parts of the world. The post As Iranians Fight Their Far-Right Government, A Narrative War Brews Elsewhere appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Why Raghav Chadha’s AI Profile Picture Became A Metaphor For His Performative Solidarity With Gig Workers
item.description: Will the names of the gig workers who risked their IDs for visibility, all to be declared as "miscreants", ever be etched in the public memory of the strike? The post Why Raghav Chadha’s AI Profile Picture Became A Metaphor For His Performative Solidarity With Gig Workers appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: The Housemaid Feminist Review: Subverting The ‘Madwoman’ Archetype And Class Exploitation
item.description: Paul Feig's adaptation 'The Housemaid' subverts the ‘madwoman’ trope and examines the intersection of class precarity and gendered violence. The post The Housemaid Feminist Review: Subverting The ‘Madwoman’ Archetype And Class Exploitation appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: History On Skin: How Dalit Leatherwork Challenges The Brahmanical Aesthetic Circle
item.description: In recent decades, leather has become a powerful Dalit symbol which does not seek sympathy but recognition. The post History On Skin: How Dalit Leatherwork Challenges The Brahmanical Aesthetic Circle appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: The Handloom As A Feminist Site: Agency, Power Relations And Systemic Challenges
item.description: Weaving and the loom become a site of economic empowerment while also underscoring that empowerment is an ongoing, sustained effort that extends beyond income generation to gradually creating systemic changes and shifting gendered attitudes, relations and norms. The post The Handloom As A Feminist Site: Agency, Power Relations And Systemic Challenges appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: ‘Kaantha’ (2025): A Film About Filmmaking That Doesn’t Quite Deliver
item.description: 'Kaantha' gives us an inside look into the unforgiving world of the film industry and its implications on filmstars who are driven to the edge of self-destruction. The post ‘Kaantha’ (2025): A Film About Filmmaking That Doesn’t Quite Deliver appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: When Women And Queer Artists Had To Become Men To Be Seen
item.description: Women’s expression was coded as too emotional, domestic, or secondary. Queer expression was sanitized or erased. The post When Women And Queer Artists Had To Become Men To Be Seen appeared first on Feminism in India.

item.title: Bhuri Bai: Mural Meets Memoir And More
item.description: Bhuri Bai’s mural is her memoir. While the entire mural looks like a single painting, which it is, it can be actually read in thirty-six parts that chronicles her journey. The post Bhuri Bai: Mural Meets Memoir And More appeared first on Feminism in India.
